info.title: LabBridge API
info.description:
Configure and automate laboratory instruments through one ESP32 bridge. Physical devices expose discoverable source, sink and scalar sensor components; prefer their common routes for portable scripts. Driver-specific routes remain available for specialized settings and compatibility.

## Typical automation sequence
1. Read node identity/boot_id and discover devices, components, actions and limits.
2. Reserve all actor devices on this node with createLease and heartbeat at least once per second. Ownership is per physical device, not per component.
3. Send a setting/output mutation with X-Lab-Lease and a new Idempotency-Key. A 202 response is only acceptance: poll Location until a terminal Operation, checking final_output and restore_pending.
4. Use valid, fresh sensor readings; preserve sign and units. Integrate only across consecutive samples with unchanged boot_id/epoch and bounded gaps.
5. Request independent STOP when finished or uncertain, verify OFF, then release the lease. Output OFF is not electrical isolation.

## Failure and retry contract
The bridge performs bounded device retries, write/readback verification and recovery. Never infer hardware success from an ATT acknowledgement, an HTTP 202 or a saved setpoint. A terminal failure can still have changed hardware. Device/component STOP requires no lease. Reconnect/reboot never resumes ON. Leases, operation IDs and idempotency keys are boot-local; do not replay an uncertain mutation after a reboot. Monotonic timestamps are not Unix time and cannot be compared across nodes/boots.

## Access and provisioning
LAN HTTP accepts Authorization: Bearer <token> for scripts or a UI password session on a trusted network. The UI redirects unauthenticated access to password login and resumes read-only discovery, never an uncertain mutation. UI passwords use salted version-two PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 verifiers with 6,000 iterations, deliberately tuned for basic protection and a login below three seconds on the ESP. Experimental 600,000-round verifiers require trusted USB password recovery; their hashes are never reinterpreted with fewer rounds. Choose the first password via the setup AP or trusted USB. HTTP is unencrypted; HTTPS with optional mTLS authentication is a separate planned feature. Obtain the API bearer secret using getManagementToken over physically trusted USB. The open LabBridge-Setup AP at 192.168.4.1 allows Wi-Fi setup/scan without bearer credentials; it does not grant laboratory control. The separate UI pages are /wifi, /devices and /dl24 (DL24M Bench). The Bench page shares the UI password session and CSRF protection and uses the same laboratory APIs; unsupported original controls remain visible but disabled. USB uses the same methods/paths with JSON-line requests {id, method, path, headers, body} and replies prefixed LABJSON; ignore other boot/log lines and correlate IDs. Target Wi-Fi PSKs are never returned.

## Local safeguards and hardware scope
Configured limits, lease expiry, measurement freshness, activation deadlines and optional external cell-temperature guards operate on the node. They supplement instrument protections and an explicit external battery test profile/wiring arrangement. Read-only sensors may omit actuator limits. Supported endpoint/pin combinations depend on the board. DL24M BLE behavior is commissioned on display Ver: 2.0; RD6018/RD6024, INA228 and Yocto physical commissioning is tracked separately. RD6018 original Wi-Fi modules connect to the ESP AP using RTU-over-TCP; use the module provisioning operations to configure them. Native Yocto USB on ESP is not implemented (use native PC USB or HTTP VirtualHub/YoctoHub).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique key per logical mutation (1..96 characters). Repeating the same method/path/semantic JSON body within this boot returns the existing operation; reusing it for different content returns 409. Retention is bounded. After an uncertain timeout or reboot, inspect state and STOP as needed instead of replaying ON.

requestBody.description: JSON request with the fields documented by the referenced schema. Unknown properties are rejected; use {} for an empty StopRequest.

put.summary: Enable or disable a physical device output
put.description:
Compatibility output control for the device driver. Enabling requires a valid lease, ready state, fresh telemetry and configured safety limits/guards. Generated clients use the regular lease header for this route; use stopDevice for explicit lease-independent shutdown after a session failure. The runtime also treats enabled=false as priority STOP. Prefer component output control for composite devices.

Returns 202 with an Operation and Location, not an instrument acknowledgement. Keep the lease alive where required and poll until terminal. Bounded device retries/readback recovery run on the bridge; callers receive a terminal failure when recovery is exhausted. Do not automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

post.description:
Request shutdown of all actors on this physical device without a lease, including after session expiry or an interrupted command. Pending work is cancelled as appropriate and OFF is verified when communication allows. Poll the operation and inspect final_output; acceptance alone does not confirm OFF. Unknown output remains a fault/recovery condition.

post.description: Acquire one exclusive lease for the listed devices on this node. Components share their physical device lease. Unknown IDs, duplicates and existing ownership are rejected. Heartbeat at least once per second; expiry or a group safety fault requests STOP for the entire group. Acquisition across multiple nodes is not atomic: unwind earlier acquisitions if another fails.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Exact quoted ETag returned by getConfiguration (for example "3"). A stale/mismatched revision returns 412; GET the current configuration before retrying a deliberate replacement.

put.summary: Validate and persist a complete configuration
put.description: Replace the complete configuration, not a partial patch. First stop all outputs and release all leases; pending restoration/shutdown also blocks replacement (409). If-Match must equal the current ETag (412 otherwise). Driver, endpoint, pin, calibration and capacity checks run before saving (422 on rejection). The node assigns the next revision and reboots about 500 ms after success; reconnect and rediscover using the new boot_id.

The setup AP is open by default; configureAccessPoint controls its security independently.

get.description: Return the command result within the current boot. Poll the Location returned by an accepted mutation until succeeded, failed or cancelled. Inspect final_output, restore_pending and error even after a terminal result. Terminal records are retained for up to five minutes in a bounded 128-entry cache; priority STOP may evict old terminal records sooner. A 404 after reboot/eviction does not prove a write was never executed.

put.description: Persist AP security and apply after the response (about 300 ms). Requires confirmed OFF/quiescent instruments, released leases and no pending Wi-Fi operation; returns 409 otherwise. AP clients disconnect and must reconnect with the new passphrase. Station credentials are unchanged. Use USB or the station address to retain management access. Requires a bearer token or UI session with X-Lab-CSRF on all HTTP interfaces, including the open AP. Independent instrument STOP remains available. Empty PSK explicitly restores the open default; no automatic fallback opens a secured AP.

parameters.description: Session-bound anti-CSRF secret for browser mutations. Required over HTTP; trusted USB bypasses browser authentication.

bearerAuth.description: Node bearer token for trusted-LAN HTTP, provisioned through physically trusted USB. USB local management is trusted without this header. Wi-Fi setup routes permit unauthenticated access only on the setup AP (open by default); laboratory routes do not. Alternatively use a UI password session cookie; cookie mutations additionally require X-Lab-CSRF. Bearer clients remain supported without cookie/CSRF headers.

browserSession.name: LabBridgeSession
browserSession.description: Boot-local opaque UI session set by loginUi; twelve-hour absolute expiry. Cookie-authenticated HTTP mutations also require same-origin JSON (where a body is used) and X-Lab-CSRF. HTTP is for trusted LAN use; it is not encrypted.

type.description: Problem type identifier; use status/detail for diagnostics rather than parsing the title.

status.description: HTTP status associated with this problem, including failures embedded in an operation.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation of the failure; wording is not a stable machine discriminator.

request_id.description: Correlation identifier when supplied by the transport.

stage.description: Driver/recovery stage where the failure was detected.

final_output.description: Last confirmed output state. unknown means shutdown has not been verified and must never be interpreted as off.

restore_pending.description: True when the original instrument settings still require recovery. New conflicting work/configuration is blocked until recovery completes.

Problem.description: Structured request or operation failure using application/problem+json. A failed write may already have changed hardware. Inspect final_output and restore_pending and request independent STOP when the outcome is uncertain.

id.description: Configured node ID; use a distinct alias/identity for each bridge in a multi-node test.

boot_id.description: Opaque identifier for this node boot. A change invalidates prior monotonic timestamps, leases and operation IDs.

board.description: Board profile that defines available transports and pin/resource restrictions.

api_version.description: Public API version implemented by this node.

NodeInfo.description: Identity and version boundary for one bridge boot. Scope device IDs to a node, and scope leases, operations and monotonic timestamps to boot_id.

voltage_v.description: Maximum permitted operating voltage in V for this actuator.

current_a.description: Maximum permitted current in A for this actuator.

power_w.description: Maximum permitted operating power in W for this actuator.

max_age_ms.description: Maximum telemetry age in milliseconds before local safety shutdown, at most 3000 ms.

max_duration_s.description: Maximum local enabled duration in seconds. A per-activation output deadline can shorten this limit.

SafetyLimits.description: Bridge-local operating envelope for an actuator. The platform requires positive voltage/current/power limits for actuators; read-only sensors may omit limits. These are additional limits, not a replacement for instrument protection or a complete battery profile.

id.description: Configured local physical device ID used in route paths.

driver.description: Registered driver module identifier; use capabilities/components to discover functions.

identity.description: Stable physical transport identity used to avoid binding two entries to the same instrument.

transport.description: Configured transport class, such as ble, uart, usb, i2c, http or gpio.

capabilities.description: Advertised device-level capability identifiers; optional features must be discovered.

state.description: unavailable: cannot communicate; ready: available; busy: command/recovery in progress; fault: a guard or recovery condition requires attention.

output.description: Aggregate physical-device output status. unknown is not OFF.

components.description: Actor and sensor descriptors exposed by this physical device.

Device.description: One physical instrument and transport/recovery identity. All its components share physical-device ownership, fault handling and lease expiry behavior.

devices.description: Configured instruments, including unavailable entries; IDs are local to this node.

DeviceList.description: Configured local physical instruments, including currently unavailable devices.

id.description: Driver-native channel ID, retained for compatibility and legacy guard bindings.

kind.description: internal is electronics/die temperature; external_probe/cell can be used for cell guarding after appropriate physical placement.

quality.description: valid: usable within freshness policy; stale: previous sample is too old; unavailable: no usable sample. Never substitute zero for invalid/missing data.

value_c.description: Measured temperature in degrees Celsius; omitted when no usable value exists.

received_ms.description: Node-monotonic milliseconds when this sample was received. Compare only within the same node and boot_id.

age_ms.description: Elapsed milliseconds since receipt, evaluated for this response. A repeated read does not freshen a cached sample.

TemperatureChannel.description: One typed temperature channel. Only fresh external_probe/cell channels qualify for cell guards; internal temperature cannot substitute for a cell probe.

channels.description: Independent typed channels with their own quality and age.

TemperatureChannels.description: Cached per-channel temperature values with independent availability and freshness.

device_id.description: Configured physical device ID, scoped to this node.

sequence.description: Provider sample sequence. Use it with boot_id/epoch to detect new samples; repeated API reads can return the same sequence.

received_ms.description: Node-monotonic milliseconds when this sample was received. Compare only within the same node and boot_id.

age_ms.description: Elapsed milliseconds since receipt, evaluated for this response. A repeated read does not freshen a cached sample.

quality.description: valid: usable within freshness policy; stale: previous sample is too old; unavailable: no usable sample. Never substitute zero for invalid/missing data.

voltage_v.description: Voltage in V. Preserve provider sign where supported.

current_a.description: Current in A. Measurements retain provider sign; targets are non-negative limits/setpoints.

power_w.description: Power in W. Measurements retain provider sign; configured limits are positive ceilings.

capacity_ah.description: Native instrument capacity counter in Ah when its scale is supported; do not assume DL24M raw counter scales are commissioned.

energy_wh.description: Native instrument energy counter in Wh when its scale is supported. Prefer traceable host integration where native scaling is uncertain.

temperature_channels.description: Typed temperature channels; an internal channel cannot stand in for a cell probe.

set_voltage_v.description: Cached voltage setpoint in V when available; this is not measured terminal voltage.

set_current_a.description: Cached current limit/target in A when available; this is not measured current.

regulation_mode.description: Observed/selected regulation mode where available: cc (constant current), cv (constant voltage), or unknown. Do not infer it solely from a setpoint.

protection_code.description: Driver-specific protection status code, not a portable cross-device enum.

boot_id.description: Opaque identifier for this node boot. A change invalidates prior monotonic timestamps, leases and operation IDs.

input_voltage_v.description: Source input supply voltage in V when supported. This is distinct from output voltage and its operating limit.

battery_voltage_v.description: Voltage in V reported by a dedicated battery-sensing input when supported. Do not infer electrical isolation or a valid battery wiring arrangement from this value.

battery_detected.description: Instrument-reported battery presence, when supported. This is telemetry, not authorization for a battery operation or proof of correct wiring.

Measurements.description: Compatibility device-level snapshot. Optional fields are present only when supported/available; absence must never be converted into a measured zero. Prefer SensorReading for new meter/composite integrations.

id.description: Opaque operation ID valid only in this boot; poll the returned Location.

device_id.description: Configured physical device ID, scoped to this node.

status.description: pending/running: unfinished; succeeded: verified completion; failed/cancelled: inspect error, final_output and restore_pending before further work.

stage.description: Diagnostic progress/recovery stage; stage strings are driver-specific.

read_attempts.description: Number of device read attempts reported by the driver, including retries.

write_attempts.description: Number of device write attempts reported by the driver, including retries.

reconnects.description: Transport reconnection attempts made during the operation.

duration_ms.description: Operation elapsed time in milliseconds as reported by the driver.

confirmed_value.description: Verified scalar result. Common component operations use confirmed_unit and expose it only on success; compatibility/device-specific operations may use raw register units.

final_output.description: Last confirmed output state. unknown means shutdown has not been verified and must never be interpreted as off.

restore_pending.description: True when the original instrument settings still require recovery. New conflicting work/configuration is blocked until recovery completes.

component_id.description: Component ID scoped to the physical device; discover it through listComponents.

confirmed_unit.description: Engineering unit for confirmed_value on a successful common component command; output uses 1 for boolean 0/1.

requested_unit.description: Engineering unit of requested_value for a common component command.

requested_value.description: Normalized common component target, for example amperes, volts, seconds or boolean 0/1.

Operation.description: Asynchronous command lifecycle. Only succeeded confirms completion; pending/running are not confirmations. Failed/cancelled operations can have physical side effects. Common component routes report requested/confirmed values in engineering units; compatibility routes can return raw driver values.

enabled.description: True requests ON; false requests OFF. Prefer independent STOP if no valid lease is available.

max_duration_ms.description: Optional local upper bound in milliseconds for this activation (100 ms..24 h), starting at acceptance. It must not exceed a configured max_duration_s; exceeding the limit is rejected, not silently clamped. This is a safety deadline, not a precision pulse timer.

OutputRequest.description: Output intent, optionally with a bridge-local deadline for this activation. Sending a setpoint never implicitly enables an output.

current_a.description: Current in A. Measurements retain provider sign; targets are non-negative limits/setpoints.

CurrentRequest.description: Current target in A: source current limit or sink CC setpoint. Schema bounds are upper contract bounds; driver precision and configured limits can be stricter.

voltage_v.description: Voltage in V. Preserve provider sign where supported.

VoltageRequest.description: Voltage target in V. Driver precision, capabilities and configured voltage/power limits may reject a value within the generic schema range.

device_ids.description: Physical device IDs to reserve together. List each device once, even if several of its actors are used.

ttl_ms.description: Heartbeat TTL in milliseconds (1000..10000, default 10000). Renew at least every second; expiry requests group shutdown.

LeaseRequest.description: Exclusive reservation of physical devices on one node. Reserve each physical device once, even when controlling several of its components.

id.description: Opaque lease ID for X-Lab-Lease; valid only within this node boot.

device_ids.description: Physical devices covered by this exclusive lease.

expires_at_ms.description: Node-monotonic heartbeat deadline in milliseconds; not a Unix timestamp.

state.description: Only active authorizes commands. stopped/expired means ownership ended; shutdown verification may still be pending.

Lease.description: Boot-local device-group ownership and heartbeat deadline. Stopping/expiry initiates group shutdown; it is not itself proof that physical outputs are OFF.

reason.description: Optional operator/application diagnostic note, at most 120 characters; does not change shutdown semantics.

StopRequest.description: Optional diagnostic reason. Send {} when no reason is needed; this body is also used by lease heartbeats and counter reset.

id.description: Stable local name used in API paths, unique within the node.

driver.description: Registered module: for example dl24m, rd60xx, gpio_interlock, ds18b20, ina228 or yocto_watt.

transport.description: Transport supported by the driver and board; incompatible combinations are rejected.

endpoint.description: Stable physical identity. For RD60xx use the canonical decimal instrument serial from registers 1/2, including for TCP; never a DHCP address or USB path. DL24M uses a BLE address, INA228 a decimal I2C address 64..79, and Yocto a YWATMK2C-... hardware serial.

pins.description: Ordered driver-specific GPIO list, explicitly allowed by the board configuration. INA228 uses [SDA, SCL]; all I2C0 instances must share the pair.

sensor_max_age_ms.description: Read-only sensor freshness limit in milliseconds; defaults to 1000 and overrides the legacy limits.max_age_ms sensor setting.

DeviceConfiguration.description: One configured physical endpoint. Select a driver-supported transport, stable identity and explicitly approved pins. Resource conflicts and invalid driver calibration are rejected before allocation. Read-only sensors need no actuator limits.

rssi_dbm.description: Received signal strength in dBm; a larger (less negative) value is stronger.

secured.description: Whether the discovered network advertises authentication; does not describe the open setup AP.

WifiNetwork.description: One network discovered by the asynchronous station scan. AP security is configured independently.

networks.description: Most recent discovered networks; may be empty while the scan is still running.

state.description: scanning: poll again; complete: cached results ready; failed: scan did not complete successfully.

WifiScan.description: Current asynchronous scan status and cached networks. Poll while scanning; an empty list does not imply a completed scan.

ssid.description: Target station network name (1..32 bytes accepted by the firmware).

psk.description: Target network secret: empty/omitted for an open network, 8..63 characters, or exactly 64 hexadecimal digits. Never returned by the API.

WifiRequest.description: Target station credentials, independent of AP security. Credentials are persisted locally and never returned by the state API.

state.description: setup: no saved station SSID; connecting: credentials exist but no station address yet (also used while retrying after disconnect); connected: station has an address. failed is reserved by the contract; the current ESP runtime keeps retrying as connecting.

hostname.description: Configured mDNS host name for the bridge.

address.description: Current station IP address when connected; omitted until the station has an address. The setup AP is separately reachable at 192.168.4.1.

ap_secured.description: Current AP authentication: true for WPA2-PSK/CCMP, false for the default open AP. The AP passphrase is never returned.

WifiState.description: Station provisioning/connection snapshot. A successful credential-save response does not imply that the station is already connected.

revision.description: Server-managed persistent configuration revision. Copy the current document for replacement; concurrency is enforced by the If-Match ETag.

node_id.description: Configured unique node name and network hostname base.

board.description: Board profile identifier; must match the running hardware profile.

devices.description: Complete desired instrument list; replacement removes omitted entries. Resource and physical-identity conflicts are rejected.

ap_ssid.description: Open ESP access-point SSID, default LabBridge-Setup. Use distinct SSIDs when splitting instruments across multiple ESPs. The AP remains password-free; its address is 192.168.4.1. The connected station LAN must use a different subnet.

NodeConfiguration.description: Complete persistent bridge configuration. Replace conditionally using the current ETag; the node assigns the next revision and reboots after accepting a replacement.

sensor_device_id.description: Sensor device on this same node, so the guard remains effective without the host/network.

channel_id.description: Temperature component ID or legacy channel ID. Must resolve to a degC external_probe/cell channel, not an internal sensor.

minimum_c.description: Lower allowed cell temperature in degrees Celsius; must be below maximum_c.

maximum_c.description: Upper allowed cell temperature in degrees Celsius; must exceed minimum_c.

max_age_ms.description: Maximum permitted probe age in milliseconds; stale/unavailable data triggers local shutdown.

CellTemperatureGuard.description: Node-local guard for a cell or external-probe temperature channel. Require fresh valid degrees-Celsius data and minimum_c < maximum_c. The guard stops the associated actor on stale/missing/out-of-range data.

active_high.description: Whether a high GPIO level energizes a selected path.

feedback_active_high.description: Whether a high feedback GPIO level means a path is closed.

break_ms.description: Minimum both-paths-open interval in milliseconds before selecting the new path (20..2000).

InterlockConfiguration.description: GPIO polarity and break-before-make configuration for a feedback-verified charge/discharge switch. Wiring and feedback must be commissioned on the actual board.

token.description: Node bearer credential for the Authorization: Bearer header on trusted-LAN HTTP requests.

ManagementToken.description: Secret bearer credential returned only through physically trusted USB management. Never publish it or include it in shared test artifacts.

AccessPointRequest.description: AP security only. Does not change station credentials or configured AP SSID. Empty PSK restores the default open AP; a non-empty printable ASCII passphrase enables WPA2-PSK/CCMP. The secret is persisted locally and never returned.

psk.description: Empty to restore the open AP, otherwise 8..63 printable ASCII characters. Supply through stdin or a private args file, not a command-line argument recorded in shell history.

UiLogin.description: Password login on the current node. JSON and same-origin browser requests only.

password.description: UI password, 12..128 Unicode characters; preserve spaces and never log or return it.

UiPasswordSetup.description: Choose and confirm the first password over the setup AP or trusted USB. No default password.

password.description: UI password, 12..128 Unicode characters; preserve spaces and never log or return it.

confirm_password.description: UI password, 12..128 Unicode characters; preserve spaces and never log or return it.

UiPasswordChange.description: Replace the UI password and invalidate all browser sessions. Network requests require the current session, CSRF header and current_password; trusted USB may omit current_password for recovery. API bearer tokens are unchanged.

password.description: UI password, 12..128 Unicode characters; preserve spaces and never log or return it.

confirm_password.description: UI password, 12..128 Unicode characters; preserve spaces and never log or return it.

current_password.description: UI password, 12..128 Unicode characters; preserve spaces and never log or return it.

AuthStatus.description: Authentication state for the current transport and browser cookie. Session secrets are private and must not be logged. Sessions last twelve hours, are boot-local and use the node monotonic clock.

password_configured.description: Whether a UI password has been configured.

setup_allowed.description: Whether first-password setup is permitted on this connection: setup AP or trusted USB, with no existing password.

authenticated.description: Whether this request has a valid browser session. Bearer access and trusted USB do not themselves create a browser session.

csrf_token.description: Secret session-bound value for X-Lab-CSRF on cookie-authenticated mutations; only present for a current session.

expires_in_ms.description: Remaining absolute browser session lifetime in node-monotonic milliseconds.

tags.name: core
tags.description: Node discovery, physical-device leases, asynchronous results, persistent configuration and Wi-Fi/USB management.

tags.name: components
tags.description: Common source, sink and scalar sensor API. Discover advertised actions and use physical-device leases for actor writes.

tags.name: dl24m
tags.description: Specialized DL24M BLE CC/settings/register operations with readback verification and restore recovery. Active non-CC modes are not commissioned.

tags.name: rd60xx
tags.description: Compatibility source setpoints via Modbus RTU. Prefer common source component routes; actual RD6024 commissioning remains open.

tags.name: gpio_interlock
tags.description: Optional feedback-verified path switching with break-before-make and both-open shutdown.

tags.name: ds18b20
tags.description: Typed temperature-channel compatibility access; common sensor readings also support these channels.

externalDocs.description: Consolidated hardware, API and protocol handbook, including supported boards and driver-specific wire formats.
